DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived

    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. However, it materially reduced 30-day retention; do not generalize it as a growth strategy.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

memory_block.body: Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.
Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.
Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.
Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. However, it materially reduced 30-day retention; do not generalize it as a growth strategy.

answer.rationale:
The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are plausibly linked, with onboarding completion the upstream driver: accounts that never finish onboarding cannot activate. Two inherited memories (memory_31, memory_86) point at signup/onboarding simplification as a durable lever, and it is the only candidate that attacks the upstream cause rather than the symptom. I am spending both verification pulls on exactly those two because they are my decision's entire evidentiary base and they may not be independent — day-12 'signup simplification' and day-52 'shortening onboarding' could easily be two consolidations of the same underlying experiment, in which case my apparent corroboration collapses to a single data point and the scale should shrink. I want the original records to check sample, segment (SMB-only vs all self-serve), and whether the reported lift was durable or a novelty spike.

I am deliberately NOT choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing being the most urgent-feeling pressure. memory_73 carries an explicit boundary condition: it lifted acquisition and revenue but materially cut 30-day retention, and prior analysts wrote down 'do not generalize as a growth strategy.' Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, discounting would buy a flattering top-line number this quarter while degrading the retention base that the objective actually measures — and it would do so in the exact segment (price-sensitive SMB) where the harm was originally observed. That inherited warning is doing real work and I am honoring it rather than overriding it because the competitive situation feels urgent. Deferring pricing also avoids teaching the org that discount-on-pressure is the reflex.

activation_messaging (memory_91) is the strongest runner-up and would address the larger raw decline, but it is in-product downstream of onboarding — pushing messaging at accounts that abandoned onboarding cannot reach them. referral_incentive (memory_57) was validated on established customers and does nothing for a top-of-funnel activation problem. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is sound but orthogonal to both declining metrics.

Downstream value risk: the real risk here is a discount habit that quietly converts long-term qualified revenue into short-term signups; secondarily, that duplicate-looking memories manufacture false confidence and justify over-scaling. Standard experiment scale with retention and time-to-value as co-primary metrics, not completion rate alone — completion is gameable by removing genuinely useful friction, which could admit low-quality accounts and reproduce the promotional-pricing failure mode by a different route. If verification shows memory_31 and memory_86 are the same experiment, or that the lift was measured only on completion without a retention readout, I will drop to a small guarded test and treat activation_messaging as the fallback.
